answer: Memory-hard presence proofs: each seat must keep a private 4 GiB table in RAM and answer one surprise "gale" window per epoch, a 30-second burst of 10,000 random lookups. The epoch seed sets a spiral visiting order, so the table can't be streamed from disk. Each lookup extends a voyage, a hash chain over the previous result, so nothing runs in parallel. A 256 GiB server holds at most 64 seats, so 500 fakes tie up 2 TiB of live RAM every epoch, caught or not.
